label: 978-r2
verdict_basis: Fast path engages in the server: the renderer now tells its processor (InputProcessingContext.mm_prefix_metadata_cache) when there is no processor cache and prefix caching is on. Through the real AsyncLLM frontend every workload's turn 2+ request goes with its repeated images stripped (6-25 KB instead of 10-41 MB), and the DS4.1-checkpoint test shows it only with --mm-processor-cache-gb 0.

The mark, round 1's bench unchanged, ABBA against candidate-54, two boots per arm: all 12 image cells are faster beyond the interval. Turn 2+ is 4.2x to 9.5x faster (1302x1302 JPEG x1 7.05x, x4 8.74x; 1920x1080 PNG 5.01x; 3840x2160 PNG x1 4.24x, x4 4.29x; 4032x3024 JPEG x4 9.51x). Turn 1 is 2% to 15% faster (JPEG 1302 x1 0.964, x4 0.959; PNG 1920 0.892; 3840 x1 0.849, x4 0.875; JPEG 4032 x4 0.981), so no cell is slower. Prompt token ids and mm hashes equal candidate-54's in every workload and turn.
Text-only requests through the same frontend (short, long, n=4), ABBA, two boots per arm: no cell slower beyond the interval (all within); a text request runs no round-2 code beyond two empty checks.

The JPEG slowdown was #978's own and is removed: the lazy-image header cache (moved decodes into the processor's thread, 3x the page faults in the HF work) now runs only with the fast path, and MultiModalHasher's multithreaded blake3 (woke the processor's thread onto Cortex-A725 cores) is reverted.

The four risks are closed with tests: a schedule-time retryable miss, a retry materializer for every sampled child, bounded marks (LRU 4096), and retries off the output handler. Round 1's fixes and #972's rollback and shielded abort hold: the gate files pass (68, 6 more than round 1), and the six new AsyncLLM tests fail on round 1's tree.

check_978_image_chat.py could not run (no live server on sp8; the command for the testbed is given). Caveat for the owner: with the recipe's process environment added to the bench (not the mark), 1920x1080 PNG turn 1 was slower beyond the interval (80.9/79.7 ms against 72.0/70.2) while the other 11 cells were faster or within; its stage diagnostic shows the processor's thread running the HF work on Cortex-A725 cores in one of two r2 boots (46 ms against 31 ms), the other boot faster than base. Production also pins the API server mostly to A725 cores (0792), which no bench here applies.

what_changed_in_round_2.fast_path_engages_in_the_server: InputProcessingContext gains mm_prefix_metadata_cache (default False); MultiModalRegistry.create_processor takes it; BaseRenderer sets it for its serving processor when there is no processor cache, prefix caching is on, the frontend has one engine (DP 1 or an external load balancer) and there is no KV or EC transfer (_uses_mm_prefix_fastpath). BaseMultiModalProcessor reads only that flag (prefix_metadata_cache_enabled) instead of ctx.vllm_config, which the server's context never carried. AsyncLLM._mm_prefix_fastpath is the processor's flag. Elsewhere (a processor cache, profiling and dummy inputs, any context without the flag) the processor is unchanged.
what_changed_in_round_2.new_images_cost_no_more: with the fast path on and no item from bytes loaded before, the processor runs its usual path (HF processor, prompt updates) while one helper thread (vllm-mm-hash) computes the hashes, then records the items' metadata; the header cache keys on SHA-256, looks new bytes up by a pre-key (length, first and last 16 KiB) and hashes them in full on a helper thread (vllm-image-digest) alongside their decode (64 KiB or more)

jpeg_finding.summary: The slowdown was #978's own, from two changes that ran with the fast path off (round 1 never engaged it in the server), and neither changed a result. (a) image.py: the validated-header cache returned repeat bytes as _LazyPILImage, which moved their decode into the processor's thread (the renderer's MM executor). From then on the HF processor's work took about three times the minor page faults (14,544 against 4,981 for a 1302x1302 JPEG request, turn 1 included: the process's allocator state changes) and ~9 ms more kernel time: 1302x1302 JPEG, turn 1 HF stage 19.1 ms against 12.2 ms. A CPU-only stage split in one thread (round 1's) cannot show this. Hashing the header key single-threaded did not remove it (img978st: 14,549 faults). (b) hasher.py: blake3 on every core (rayon). The processor's thread blocks on the pool and is woken onto whichever core is free, often a Cortex-A725 (cpus 0-4, 10-14), and the HF work after it ran there: 1302x1302 JPEG turn 2+, HF 13.2 ms with 42% of samples on A725 cores against 8.9 ms (h978 alone, raw/jpeg-bisect/diag1); for a 0.9 MB JPEG the pool saved less than its wake-up (hash 1.6 ms wall against 1.26 ms single-threaded). Each change alone reproduced part of round 1's 1302 JPEG loss (bisect1: base 22.3/24.8 ms turn 1, image.py alone 31.0, hasher alone 27.6, round 1 40.9/41.8). In round 2 the same placement effect bit the multithreaded hash's large-image gain: with it, 1920x1080 PNG turn 1 was bimodal (54.8 or 71.2 ms against base 58.8; HF 41 ms with two thirds on A725 cores), so it was removed (raw/superseded/mark2, mark3, diag6).
jpeg_finding.fix: the validated-header cache is on only with the fast path (set_validated_image_meta_cache_enabled, set by the renderer), where a repeat image is never decoded; without the fast path loading is candidate-54's; MultiModalHasher is candidate-54's again (hashes on its own thread; mm hashes never depended on threading); new images under the fast path take the processor's usual path with their hashes computed alongside on one helper thread
jpeg_finding.method: bisection by file over candidate-54 (arms h978, img978, img978st, r1st) with round 1's bench, then serving_stage_diag.py: round 1's bench with each stage wrapped at runtime (wall, thread CPU, system time, minor faults via getrusage(RUSAGE_THREAD), share of samples on A725 cores via sched_getcpu)

stripped_item_loses_coverage_before_sche.how: Scheduler._try_schedule_encoder_inputs: when an encoder input that came without data must run and its encoder output is not cached, it borrows another live request's data; failing that it records the miss (stripped_mm_misses) and leaves the request unscheduled this step (num_new_tokens 0), never scheduling the encoder without data (which made the worker raise 'Encoder cache miss' and stop the engine). update_from_output finishes those requests with FINISHED_ERROR and mm_cache_miss_hashes, beside the grammar-error path. The frontend restarts a request that has returned nothing yet (RequestState.is_prefilling) with all its items' data under the same id; one that already returned output (preempted after its first token) ends with the error, since a restart would repeat that output. Add-time verification and its encoder-cache pin are unchanged.

only_first_sampled_child_keeps_retry_mat.how: _prepare_mm_features_for_prefix_cache replaces a stripped item in a copy of the child's own mm_features list (dataclasses.replace) instead of setting f.data on the feature specs the children share, so each child sees the lazy item, strips it and keeps its own materializer (keyed by feature index)

unbounded_p1_identifier_tracking.how: SentMMIdentifiers: an LRU of MAX_SENT_MM_IDENTIFIERS = 4096 identifiers (the processor's metadata cache holds 512 items; only those can go stripped); a stripped item refreshes its mark; a dropped mark only means the item is sent with its data again

retry_materializes_on_the_output_handler.how: the output handler starts each retry as its own task (AsyncLLM._mm_retry_tasks, cancelled at shutdown) and goes on; the task materializes all stripped items on the MM executor with the processor's torch thread setting, skips the resubmission if the request was aborted meanwhile, marks and resends, and finishes the request with an error if that fails

also_closed.streaming_input_requests: always send their items' data, since they cannot be restarted from their first chunk (test_streaming_input_items_are_sent_with_their_data)
also_closed.a_retry_that_could_miss_again: a retry resends every stripped item of the request, not only the missed ones
also_closed.dead_ced_lookup: the unused getattr(self.scheduler, 'ced_Prompt_replay_tokens', 0) in _verify_or_resolve_stripped_mm_features is removed; get_computed_blocks already caps the hit at the replay boundary

remaining: A cancelled materialization keeps running on the single-worker MM executor until it ends (unchanged from round 1).

A request preempted after its first token whose stripped item is no longer held anywhere ends with an error instead of being served; candidate-54 would have served it from the data it carried. It needs eviction of both the encoder output and the prefix blocks while the request is preempted.
With KV connectors a finished request's blocks can be freed late; the fast path is off with any KV or EC transfer, so the same-id resubmission never meets that.
